reasoning: Kept the three non-overlapping corrections: recognize quoted cloze prompts even without an ellipsis, refine name granularity without overriding relevant full-name cues, and infer the intended relation for terse work-title clues rather than defaulting to a creator. Each edit is supported by one of the two source patches. [optimizer-ranked: selected 2/3 edits]

edits.target: - If a prompt consists only of a work title and year, do not answer with its generic type (such as “film”). Look for a principal person explicitly and centrally associated with that work in the context, such as its director, author, or creator, and answer with that person only when the association is clear. If the context offers no clear intended relation, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.
edits.content: - For a terse work-title clue, do not answer with the work’s generic type or assume that the creator is wanted. Use the wording and context to infer the intended relation: if the clue frames a work as an adaptation, retelling, or remake and points to its source, return that source work; return a creator only when that relation is clearly intended. If no intended relation is supported, treat the prompt as underdetermined rather than guessing.

edits.target: - When an ellipsis marks omitted words in a title or phrase, use context to recover and return the missing continuation. Prefer a completion that fits the whole fragment over a prominent work or entity that matches only a shorter substring.
edits.content: - If a quoted line or phrase is cut off and the prompt asks what comes next (for example, by ending with “this”), treat it as a cloze: return the immediate missing word or phrase, not the source work’s title or author. Use the whole quoted fragment to resolve the continuation.

ranking_details.reasoning: Edit 2 adds a meaningful relation check that prevents assuming a creator is wanted when the clue points to a source work. Edit 0 fills a narrower gap by distinguishing a requested continuation from the title or author of a quoted source. Edit 1 mostly restates existing name-form and granularity guidance.
